item.name: Interrupted-turn memory sync suppression
item.contract: Interrupted or cancelled turns cannot flush partial observations into GONCHO or external Honcho-compatible memory
item.degraded_mode: Memory status reports skipped or interrupted sync attempts without promoting partial facts to recall.
ready_when: The turn-finalization path can tell a normal completion from an interrupt, cancellation, or client disconnect.
not_ready_when: The slice rewrites extraction, recall, or provider-plugin storage instead of only gating sync/finalization on interrupted turns.
acceptance: Interrupted turns record a skipped-sync reason and do not create new GONCHO conclusions.
Completed turns still sync/extract normally.
Operator status can distinguish skipped interrupted sync from extractor failures.
item.note: TDD landed: interrupted turns are marked as skipped with reason=interrupted, stay out of extractor and Honcho-compatible turn reads, and create no goncho_conclusions; completed turns still mark ready and extract normally. Fixtures cover internal/memory/interrupted_sync_test.go plus skipped-row guards in the memory session catalog and GONCHO service. Verified with go test ./internal/kernel ./internal/memory ./internal/goncho -count=1.
done_signal: Interrupted-turn fixtures prove partial memory observations are skipped while completed turns still sync.

item.name: SillyTavern persona and group-chat mapping fixtures
item.contract: Goncho maps Honcho SillyTavern peer modes, session naming, enrichment modes, and group-chat participants without widening recall or leaking the internal goncho name
item.degraded_mode: Host mapping evidence reports unsupported SillyTavern panel knobs or missing peer/session identifiers instead of silently merging personas or group characters.
ready_when: Honcho host integration compatibility fixtures already map baseline SillyTavern chat-instance sessions, recall modes, host-scoped config, and honcho_* external tool names.
not_ready_when: The slice adds a SillyTavern extension, imports Node/browser code, calls hosted Honcho, or changes Goncho persistence instead of fixture-locking host mapping decisions.
acceptance: Peer mode fixtures distinguish one shared user peer from separate persona-scoped peers without changing the default Goncho workspace.
Session naming fixtures cover auto per-chat, per-character, and custom session names, including reset/orphan evidence for new chats.
Group-chat fixtures register one peer per character and lazy-add mid-chat characters instead of collapsing to one group peer.
Context-only, reasoning, and tool-call enrichment modes map to prompt context, honcho_chat-style reasoning, and tool exposure with explicit degraded evidence for unsupported modes.
item.note: TDD landed: `internal/goncho/sillytavern_mapping_test.go` fixture-locks Honcho SillyTavern peer modes, auto/per-character/custom session naming with reset/orphan evidence, group-chat one-peer-per-character mapping with lazy mid-chat additions, context/reasoning/tool-call enrichment mapping, and degraded evidence for unsupported panel knobs or missing peer/session identifiers. The mapper stays pure Goncho host evidence: no SillyTavern extension, no Node/browser imports, no hosted Honcho calls, no persistence changes, and external tool evidence preserves honcho_* names including honcho_chat.
done_signal: SillyTavern mapping fixtures prove persona/session/group-chat decisions and enrichment-mode degradation while external tools keep honcho_* names.

provenance.note: Honcho defines host-facing SillyTavern behavior; Gormes maps it into internal Goncho fixtures and operator evidence.

item.name: Cross-chat deny-path fixtures
item.contract: Same-chat default recall with explicit user-scope widening
item.degraded_mode: Memory status and operator evidence report unresolved, conflicting, or denied cross-chat identity bindings.
ready_when: Honcho-compatible scope/source tool schema is complete and exposes source allowlist semantics.
not_ready_when: Deny-path fixtures are mixed with operator evidence rendering in the same slice.
acceptance: Unknown user bindings stay same-chat.
Conflicting user bindings deny user-scope widening.
Allowed user-scope searches include source allowlist evidence.
item.note: TDD landed: recall and session-search fixtures now deny user-scope widening when the current chat binding is unknown, unresolved, or conflicting; denied paths fall back to same-chat/session behavior, and allowed user-scope GONCHO hits preserve origin_source evidence for source allowlists.
done_signal: Cross-chat recall fixtures prove unknown and conflicting identities cannot widen search scope.

item.name: Cross-chat operator evidence
item.contract: Memory and Goncho status expose operator-readable evidence for allowed, denied, and degraded cross-chat recall decisions
item.degraded_mode: Status and dry-run output report unresolved user bindings, conflicting chat bindings, source allowlists, and host mapping gaps before recall widens.
ready_when: Cross-chat deny-path fixtures are complete, Honcho-compatible scope/source tool schemas are visible, and SillyTavern host mapping drift is either fixture-locked or explicitly degraded.
not_ready_when: The slice changes recall ranking, creates new memory storage tables, or ports dialectic reasoning instead of only rendering existing allow/deny evidence.
blocked_by: SillyTavern persona and group-chat mapping fixtures
acceptance: Allowed user-scope recall reports resolved user_id, source allowlist, session/chat source, and number of widened sessions considered.
Denied recall reports unknown, unresolved, or conflicting identity reason and names the same-chat fallback scope.
Goncho context/search dry-run output preserves origin_source evidence for returned hits.
`gormes memory status` or an equivalent diagnostics path renders the evidence without exposing raw SQL rows.
item.note: TDD landed: internal/memory/cross_chat_operator_evidence_test.go pins allowed and denied cross-chat recall evidence with resolved user_id, source allowlists, session/chat source, current binding details, widened-session counts, and same-chat fallback reasons for unresolved, unknown, or conflicting identity. Goncho search/context results now carry scope_evidence and preserve origin_source on returned hits, while gormes goncho doctor --scope user --sources renders the evidence without exposing raw SQL rows. The SillyTavern persona/group-chat mapping gate was fixture-locked before this closeout, so host mapping gaps remain explicit degraded evidence instead of being hidden by generic cross-chat status.
done_signal: Cross-chat evidence fixtures prove allowed and denied recall paths produce operator-readable user/source/session diagnostics.

provenance.note: Gormes owns the operator evidence surface; upstream Honcho/Hermes compatibility defines the host and tool semantics that evidence must not obscure.

item.name: Agent-controlled memory retention with importance scoring
item.contract: The agent assigns importance scores to memories at store time and can adjust them later. Retention policy uses importance × recency decay curve. Low-importance old memories are candidates for summarization or forgetting. The agent periodically reviews and prunes.
source_refs: Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023) recency+importance+relevance retrieval
ready_when: Goncho supports importance scoring on entries
not_ready_when: No importance metadata on memory entries
acceptance: Agent assigns importance 0.0-1.0 at storage time
Retrieval scoring: α·recency + β·importance + γ·relevance
Decay curve reduces importance over time unless reinforced
Periodic review identifies low-importance candidates
Agent can promote/demote importance via update_memory tool
item.note: Complete: TDD expanded `internal/goncho/importance_scorer.go` so ranking uses `α·recency + β·effective_importance + γ·relevance`, where effective importance is the agent-assigned importance after recency decay. `internal/goncho/decay.go` adds retention review candidates with summarize/forget actions for old low-effective-importance memories. `LocalMarkdownMemoryStore.Retrieve` now ranks active scoped memories through the shared scorer instead of raw SQL importance ordering, while retaining nonmatching memories in storage. `update_memory` now accepts optional `importance` so the agent can promote or demote entries after storage; descriptors expose the same field. Focused tests prove store-time importance, retrieval ranking, decay candidate review, and update-time importance adjustment.
done_signal: Importance tests prove scoring affects retrieval ranking and decay reduces old unused memories
